title: Remember the OS window position, size and maximized state across restarts
body:
Foreman always opens at a default 1280x800 wherever Windows puts it (src/main.rs fn main: ViewportBuilder::default().with_inner_size([1280.0, 800.0]).with_decorations(false)). Make it reopen where it was closed: same outer position and inner size, and maximized if it was maximized, with the un-maximized normal rect still remembered. docs/workspace-persistence.md lists "OS main-window position/size" as Out of v1; this card is that follow-up.

APPROACH (decided — if you find it wrong, `kanban block` with the reason rather than switching silently):
- Native, through the existing settings layer: a new Option<WindowGeometry> field on struct Settings (src/config.rs; keep #[serde(default)]; precedent: panel_width/panel_dock live in settings.json, not workspace.json). File-only, no settings-menu row — state that in the field doc comment. Follow .claude/skills/foreman-config-and-flags/SKILL.md "How to add a new persisted setting".
- Do NOT enable eframe's `persistence` cargo feature. Verified against eframe-0.34.3 in the cargo registry: it adds the `ron` crate, writes <RoamingAppData>\foreman\data\app.ron resolved via SHGetKnownFolderPath (ignores the APPDATA env var, so scripts/run-dev.ps1's sandbox would not isolate it and a dev build would overwrite the user's real position), saves on a 30 s autosave thread without config.rs's atomic write + corrupt-file backup, and its Windows clamp assumes a 32 px title bar this undecorated window does not have.
- Store: outer position in PHYSICAL pixels (plus the pixels-per-point it was captured at), inner size in logical points, maximized: bool. Capture per frame in App::update from ctx.input(|i| i.viewport()) — outer_rect/inner_rect are in points, multiply by native_pixels_per_point. Persist through the existing debounce (font_dirty_at / FONT_SAVE_DEBOUNCE in src/main.rs) and flush in App::flush_all so quit and update-restart both write it.
- Restore in fn main before eframe::run_native: with_inner_size + with_maximized on the ViewportBuilder (winit 0.30.13 applies with_maximized after CreateWindowExW, so the builder's position/size become the normal rect that un-maximize restores to). Position: with_position takes LOGICAL points and winit scales them by the DPI of wherever Windows first placed the window (CW_USEDEFAULT), so mixed-DPI setups drift; ViewportCommand::OuterPosition goes through as PHYSICAL pixels. Pick one: with_position (physical / primary-monitor scale) with a first-frame OuterPosition correction when they differ, or create hidden and position before Visible(true). Test the choice on this machine and document it.

HAZARDS (each is a Done-when line):
- Minimized: winit's outer_position() is a raw GetWindowRect, so a minimized window reports the -32000,-32000 iconic placement, and is_maximized() reads false while minimized. Never sample geometry while viewport().minimized == Some(true); while maximized update only the flag and keep the last normal rect.
- Off-screen: neither winit nor Windows clamps a restored position; a monitor unplugged since last run leaves the window invisible. Validate the saved rect against the current monitors before applying it (windows-sys MonitorFromRect/EnumDisplayMonitors need the Win32_Graphics_Gdi feature on the existing dep; GetSystemMetrics virtual-screen bounds are already available via Win32_UI_WindowsAndMessaging). Fall back to the current default placement when validation fails.
- Keep validate/clamp a pure function (saved geometry + monitor rects -> Option<geometry>) with table tests; Settings::sanitize must drop non-finite, negative, or absurd values so a hand-edited file cannot create a 0x0 or 1e9 window.
- The close-confirm path (close_requested + CancelClose in App::update) and on_exit -> flush_all must keep working; the debounced write must already be on disk before a hard kill.

DONE WHEN:
- Move + resize, quit via the chrome X, relaunch: same outer position (within a few px) and size. Maximize, quit, relaunch: opens maximized; un-maximize returns to the remembered normal rect.
- Minimize then quit: next launch is NOT at -32000; the normal rect is restored.
- Seed settings.json with a rect on a non-existent monitor (e.g. x = 20000): window comes up visible at the default placement and the bad value is replaced on the next save.
- Old settings.json without the field loads with defaults; a file with the field round-trips; unknown fields still ignored; sanitize rejects garbage geometry (mirror the existing serde tests in src/config.rs).
- No write per frame or per drag event: one write per quiet period plus the exit flush.
- scripts/run-dev.ps1 instances (APPDATA redirected to target\agent\appdata) read/write their own settings.json, never the user's.
- cargo build --target-dir target/agent adds no new warnings; cargo test --target-dir target/agent is green.
- docs/settings-persistence.md gains the field and the gotchas (minimized sentinel, with_position DPI scaling, off-screen clamp, why not eframe persistence); docs/workspace-persistence.md: replace the Out-of-v1 row and extend the Persistence map.

GUI VERIFICATION WITHOUT THE MOUSE: scripts/run-dev.ps1 -Path <your worktree> launches a sandboxed instance; seed its settings.json, launch, read the window rect back with Win32 GetWindowRect from PowerShell (Add-Type P/Invoke), close with -Kill. Or ask the human to confirm with build-screenshot. Never Stop-Process foreman by name — you are likely running inside foreman.

Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent config:: then cargo test --target-dir target/agent (the integration queue runs the full suite per .foreman/integrate.json).
